NameDrop engineering vs zh-Hans listing copy — two different jobs

Teams assume Apple's NameDrop rollout covers storefront language. iOS, system frameworks, and Connect actually separate proximity contact behavior from product-page copy:

  • NameDrop & Contact poster — system feature that lets two iPhones or Apple Watches exchange contact cards when brought together. Controls in-device contact sharing — not App Store language.
  • Nearby Interaction & proximity APIs — frameworks some apps use for device-to-device ranging and tap-to-connect UX. Your listing may mention tap-to-exchange; building proximity sessions is engineering work, not Connect metadata.
  • MultipeerConnectivity & Bonjour — custom peer-discovery and P2P transfer stacks. Separate from the zh-Hans description paragraph that explains contact exchange to buyers.
  • CNContactStore & ContactsUI — address-book read and write APIs when a exchanged card lands in Contacts. Configuring contact persistence is engineering — AppLocale does not touch it.
  • AirDrop settings & Bring Devices Together — system toggle under Settings → General → AirDrop that enables NameDrop. Your listing may reference the feature; toggling portal settings is outside AppLocale scope.
  • Pricing and Availability → China — makes the app downloadable on the China App Store. Separate from language rows.
  • App Store tab → Chinese (Simplified) localization — independent row for title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshots, and caption lines. Empty or English here means China buyers see English fallback regardless of NameDrop support in the binary.

A working NameDrop or contact-exchange story and a localized China listing are both required when you sell on the China storefront — neither replaces the other.

NameDrop-specific listing copy — what translates differently

Contact-exchange listings use vocabulary general utility guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers describe Apple's NameDrop feature — not a literal paste of US marketing:

NameDrop phrasing

US pages use "NameDrop", "Share contact with NameDrop", "Exchange contact info", or "Bring iPhones together." Apple's official Simplified Chinese support vocabulary uses 名片投送 for the system feature. Chinese tech coverage and buyer search also use 轻碰传联系人 and 姓名投送 for proximity contact sharing. AppLocale aligns phrasing with Apple's consumer-facing terms while keeping your app's voice — not inventing NameDrop capabilities your app does not support.

Share vs Receive only

Screenshot overlays differ by exchange mode — mutual share-and-receive, receive-only at events, or share a specific phone number or email from your contact poster. Chinese buyers expect concise action labels: 共享联系人 for share, 仅接收 for receive only, 交换名片 for mutual exchange. Mixing English "Receive only" with Chinese body copy on the same frame looks inconsistent.

Contact poster vs contact card

iOS 17+ Contact poster and photo-and-poster UI appear on many NameDrop marketing screenshots. zh-Hans overlays may use 联系人海报 or 我的名片 where it matches your frames — distinct from generic Add to Contacts save flows covered on the Add to Contacts guide.

Do not conflate with AirDrop file send

NameDrop is part of the AirDrop family in Settings, but listing copy for contact exchange should not reuse Send with AirDrop file-transfer paragraphs meant for 隔空投送 document send. If your app does both, scope each screenshot frame accurately — contact poster glow on one frame, file send on another.

Subtitle and keyword packing

The 30-character subtitle and 100-character keyword field need contact-exchange search terms Chinese buyers type — see Simplified Chinese keywords & subtitle for field mechanics. Terms like 名片投送, 轻碰传联系人, 交换联系人, and 姓名投送 each signal different intent from AirDrop file-transfer or Add to Contacts keywords.

  • Assuming NameDrop integration localizes automatically — proximity flow shipped; zh-Hans row never added or left blank
  • Only translating the description — subtitle, keywords, and screenshot caption lines still English
  • Reusing US NameDrop badges verbatim — Latin "Share contact with NameDrop" badges on zh-Hans screenshots signal an unfinished localization
  • Cloning AirDrop file-transfer copy — 隔空投送 paragraphs pasted where NameDrop contact-poster marketing belongs; see AirDrop listing (zh-Hans) for file-send scope
  • Cloning Add to Contacts copy — Save contact and New contact language where the hero story is tap-two-phones NameDrop; see Add to Contacts listing (zh-Hans)
  • Conflating listing copy with setup instructions — description explains how to enable Bring Devices Together in Settings instead of what the buyer gets; setup instructions belong in support docs, not AppLocale scope
  • Translating the in-app permission string only — system NameDrop sheet may show Chinese from iOS while the App Store product page stays English
  • Ignoring caption fields per localization — zh-Hans screenshot set uploaded but overlay text fields never saved; see Screenshot captions in Simplified Chinese
  • Expecting AppLocale to implement Nearby Interaction or CNContactStore — proximity APIs, MultipeerConnectivity, and address-book write logic are outside listing rewrite
